ai.title: Move user instructions to top of agent message stack
ai.summary: Relocates `userInstructions` from the bottom of the `agentMessages` array to the top in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. This ensures instruction priority is maintained regardless of message history trimming logic. The change also removes redundant `lastAssistantMessage` trimming and reorganizes context injection.

eli5.text: The agent now receives a fresh copy of its instructions every time it thinks, placed at the very end of its context so the most important guidance stays top of mind even if older conversation gets cut off. This also removes old code that tried to trim a previous assistant message, which no longer fits the new flow. The change is live in the backend as of today.

ai.title: Add saveAgentRequest debug helper
ai.summary: Adds `saveAgentRequest` in `backend/src/system-prompt/save-agent-request.ts` to write prompt state to disk. `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` gates agent context and user instructions on `prompt` presence and wires the helper behind a `debugPromptCaching` flag. Helper serializes system and messages with cache control to `system-prompts/`.

eli5.text: A developer added a hidden debugging switch that, when turned on, writes out a snapshot of the assistant's current prompt and instructions to a file on disk so the team can inspect what the assistant was told in a given moment. The snapshot is gated behind a flag set to off by default, so nothing changes for you today, but when enabled it saves the system prompt and recent messages into a local folder named system-prompts for later review. The same change also makes the assistant's context and user instructions only appear when an actual prompt is present, which is a behind-the-scenes safety tweak that does not affect how you see responses right now.

ai.title: Relax fast-rewrite test diff size threshold
ai.summary: The `linesChanged` assertion in `backend/src/__tests__/fast-rewrite.test.ts` now allows up to 10 lines instead of 5. This change addresses flakiness in the `rewriteWithOpenAI` test suite caused by strict diff size limits. The update is internal, affecting only the backend test configuration.

eli5.text: The system now allows rewrite tests to produce slightly larger diffs before failing, increasing the acceptable change threshold from five to ten lines. This is only used by the testing tools internally and does not affect anything you see or use directly. The change is live today as part of the current test configuration.

ai.title: Remove verbose agentContext debug logs
ai.summary: Deleted `logger.debug` calls for 'Updated agent context' in `main-prompt.ts` and 'Updated context' in `tools.ts`. Refactored `websocket-action.ts` to spread `params` instead of manually listing quota fields in the 'Sending usage info' log. Reduces noise in backend logs without altering functional behavior.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes systems that run the assistant kept printing too many routine status notes into the operational logs, cluttering them with repeated updates about context changes and resource limits. The change trims out the less useful of those debug messages, so if you ever look at the logs you will see fewer lines of repetitive noise and the remaining entries will be easier to find. It does not change anything the assistant does or how it responds.

ai.title: Document model stack in FAQ and advanced docs
ai.summary: Added explicit model usage documentation to `web/src/content/advanced/what-models.mdx` and `web/src/content/help/faq.mdx`. Clarified the multi-model stack: Claude Sonnet (primary coding), Gemini Flash (file retrieval), Relace AI speculative decoding (rewrites), o3-mini (fallback), and gpt-4o-mini (trivial tasks). Scope limited to Web documentation surfaces.

eli5.text: The help documents and advanced guides now explain which AI models power your project: a main coding assistant handles most of the work, a fast search tool finds the right files, a quick-rewrite engine speeds up edits, and two smaller models take over as backup or for simple tasks. The explanation also notes that switching between modes can change which models are used to balance speed and cost. If you read those pages, you will see a clearer breakdown of how the different AIs cooperate behind the scenes.

ai.title: Add Relace rerank endpoint wrapper
ai.summary: Implemented rerank function in backend/src/llm-apis/relace-api.ts calling https://ranker.endpoint.relace.run/v1/code/rank. Converts FileWithPath inputs to Relace format, sends prompt as query, and parses string array response. Includes 100s timeout, error handling returning original file order, and telemetry logging via saveMessage for non-test users. New types RankedFile and FileWithPath exported.

eli5.text: The assistant can now ask an external ranking service to sort your code files by relevance to your prompt before returning them, and this sorting happens behind the scenes whenever you paste in code and ask a question. If that service is slow or fails, the assistant still shows your original files in the order you provided them. The assistant now also records how much it used this service for its own internal tracking. This is already active today.

ai.title: Force display of explicitly requested files in context
ai.summary: Modified `getFileVersionUpdates` to include `options.requestedFiles` in the returned `newFiles` list, even if the file was already present in `previousFilePaths`. This ensures files explicitly requested by the assistant are re-sent, working around the model's inability to recognize existing context. Scope limited to `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. The logic now merges `newFilesWithoutRequestedFiles` with `options.requestedFiles` using `uniq`.

eli5.text: When you (the AI assistant) explicitly ask to see a particular file, the system will now always show it to you again, even if that file was already shown to you earlier in the same conversation. The developers noted that the assistant can't reliably recognize that a file is already in its context, so this works around that limitation by re-sending the file each time it is requested. This affects only the internal prompt-building logic and only applies to files you actively request, files you never asked for won't be re-sent. This fix went live on 2025-03-27.

ai.title: Enable Gemini stream usage stats
ai.summary: Added stream_options: {include_usage: true} to Gemini streaming API calls. This ensures usage statistics are returned alongside streamed responses. The change applies to backend/src/llm-apis/gemini-api.ts.

eli5.text: When you interact with the assistant using the Gemini model, you now receive accurate usage statistics alongside the streamed responses. This means the token counts (input and output) are now properly tracked even during streaming, so you get a complete picture of resource consumption rather than missing data. The system now explicitly requests these stats to be included in every streaming call, ensuring consistent monitoring and billing accuracy.

ai.title: Refine heuristic for new file necessity
ai.summary: Updated prompt logic in `check-new-files-necessary.ts` to improve detection of when to load new files. Added positive triggers for topic shifts and explicit mentions of new functions; clarified negative triggers for greetings and simple commands. Scope limited to backend file-finding heuristics. Refines decision boundaries for `YES`/`NO` classification.

eli5.text: When you interact with the assistant, a behind-the-scenes system decides whether to open and read relevant files based on your message. That decision logic was fine-tuned so it reacts more cleanly to topic shifts and mentions of specific functions, while staying quieter for greetings and simple commands. The change only touches how the assistant gathers context internally, so most users will just notice slightly smarter file handling with no visible interface changes.

ai.title: Add Discord API integration and slash commands
ai.summary: New Discord bot integration via `/api/discord/interactions` endpoint handling slash commands like `/link <email>`. Requests verified using ed25519 signatures with in-memory rate limiting (5 requests/minute/user) and ephemeral responses for privacy. Database schema updated with `discord_id` column (migration `0011_familiar_ezekiel_stane.sql`) to link Discord accounts to user profiles. Covers Web API route, rate-limiter, command registration script, and environment variables (`DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY`, `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`, `DISCORD_APPLICATION_ID`).

eli5.text: You can now link your Discord account to your existing profile by typing a slash command like /link <email> inside any Discord server where the bot is present. The bot verifies your request using Discord's signature, limits each person to five commands per minute, and replies only to you so others can't see your email or response. Behind the scenes, a new column in the user database stores your Discord ID, and the bot responds with messages that disappear after a short time to keep your information private. The developers note this integration only handles slash commands today, listening for new messages or member joins would require additional setup in the future.

ai.title: Refine file request prompt and token counting scope
ai.summary: Split token counting for file requests into messagesForFileRequest. Updated check-new-files-necessary.ts criteria to trigger on single user messages. Modified getFileVersionUpdates to skip readFilesMessage when requestedFiles is empty. Affects backend/src/main-prompt.ts and backend/src/find-files/check-new-files-necessary.ts.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to read files for a coding task, it now only sends the messages that are actually needed for that file-picking step, instead of reshuffling your earlier instructions into the request. This means the assistant won't show you a 'read these files' prompt unless your request actually involves files, and it stops including your original instructions in the file-request reasoning. If you're using the assistant for code, you might notice it asks for fewer files or asks sooner on simple follow-ups, since the trigger now fires on single user messages.

ai.title: Discord interactions use flags 64
ai.summary: Replaced `ephemeral: true` with `flags: 64` in `web/src/app/api/discord/interactions/route.ts`. Aligns with Discord API standard for ephemeral messages. Updated `authentication.knowledge.md` to document storing Discord IDs over usernames.

eli5.text: When you type a command in Discord that the tool doesn't fully recognize, like asking for help, sending a message too fast, or linking your account, the reply you get now appears using Discord's newer system for private messages. As a result, those responses will still show only to you in the channel exactly as they did before, but the way they're marked as private on Discord's side has shifted to the standard method. You shouldn't notice any visual difference, but the change aligns with how Discord now expects apps to request private replies. Additionally, the team updated their internal notes to clarify that user accounts are identified by permanent Discord IDs instead of usernames, since usernames can change over time.

eli5.text: When you link your Discord account, you now automatically receive the 'Verified' role on the server, so you can see and access channels restricted to verified members. Behind the scenes, the system now uses a fixed identifier for that role instead of leaving it undefined, and the message replies sent back to Discord now have consistent formatting in one spot behind the scenes. This only affects the linking flow for people already registered with Codebuff, and the role assignment is only active after you complete the link command.

ai.title: VERIFIEDROLEID in Discord interactions route changed to string
ai.summary: VERIFIED_ROLE_ID in `web/src/app/api/discord/interactions/route.ts` changed from number to string literal. Discord snowflake IDs exceed JS Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, risking precision loss in numeric representation. Affects Discord interaction request verification logic.

eli5.text: The Discord bot's check for your verified-role membership now treats the internal role identifier as plain text instead of a number. This matters because Discord's identifiers are so large that JavaScript can lose precision when they're stored as numbers, which could occasionally make a correctly verified user fail the check. If you looked at the bot's verification code, you'd see the role identifier written in quotes. The fix is already in place today, so verified-role checks on Discord interactions are now reliably accurate.
